topic: Cancellation confirmed + post-cancellation domestic pivot and separate 2026 export corridor
wiki_text: The Djibouti FLNG Terminal (the Poly-GCL/GCL liquefaction-and-export terminal proposed at Damerjog to monetize Ethiopian Ogaden Basin gas) remains cancelled. Ethiopia's Energy Outlook 2025, released in June 2025, officially cancelled the planned Ogaden (Calub/Hilala) gas extraction and the Ethiopia–Djibouti pipeline-to-LNG-export scheme, citing failure to secure financing and slow implementation; Poly-GCL's resource license had already been terminated in September 2022. As of mid-2026 no developer has revived this export terminal. Ethiopia has instead pivoted Ogaden gas to DOMESTIC use — a 200,000 m³ skid-mounted LNG plant in Ethiopia's Ogaden Basin was commissioned on 2 October 2025 for domestic power/industry/fertilizer, and in March 2026 Dangote signed a ~US$4.2bn 25-year gas-supply agreement sourcing Calub gas via a 108 km pipeline for a domestic plant. Separately, in May 2026 Djibouti's government, Ethiopian Investment Holdings and the Dangote Group announced a two-phase Ethiopia–Djibouti oil-and-gas export corridor (refined-products pipeline, then crude-oil and natural-gas export pipelines via Djibouti) — a pipeline/liquid-bulk-depot project with no LNG liquefaction or export-terminal component, and distinct from this cancelled FLNG terminal.
